cohort: The study included 20 aborted women in the first trimester of pregnancy infected with Toxoplasma gondii and 6 women with normal births as a control group, aged 15-45 years.
finding: Infected placentas with Toxoplasmosis showed various histopathological changes, including necrosis, lymphocyte infiltrations, hydropic degeneration, fibrinoid deposition, vacuolation, hemorrhage, and the presence of the parasitic stage, compared to healthy placental tissues.
cross-section timing: Placental tissue samples were collected from aborted women (in the first trimester) and a normal birth control group between October 2016 and January 2017.
